newsitem.title: EGYPT: Gunmen kill two policemen in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill two policemen in south Egypt.

text.p: Gunmen shot dead two plainclothes policemen and wounded five others when they ambushed a police car in southern Egypt on Friday, security sources said.

They said the attack took place near the town of Dayrut, 315 km (195 miles) south of Cairo, as the policemen checked an annonymous tip on the whereabouts of fugitives. None of the policemen were wearing uniforms.
Police Captains Abdellah Mohammed Hamdan, 30, and Ayman Samir Zaki, 25, were killed in the attack, the sources said.
Police in Dayrut have yet to identify the gunmen.
The Moslem militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) is waging a low-level guerrilla war against policemen in southern Egypt as part of its anti-government campaign.
Militants want to set up a strict Islamic state.
More than 1,000 people, mostly militants and policemen, have been killed since 1992.
